differences.title: 1. COMMUNICATION DIRECTION
differences.leftDesc: Server pushes updates to the client. Client cannot send messages back directly.
differences.rightDesc: Full duplex communication. Both client and server can send messages freely.

differences.title: 2. PROTOCOL
differences.leftDesc: Built over HTTP/2, leveraging existing infrastructure and security.
differences.rightDesc: New protocol, established handshake over HTTP, then upgrades to persistent connection.

differences.title: 3. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Each message is independent. Server doesn't need to maintain client-specific state.
differences.rightDesc: Connection is persistent, allowing server to maintain connection state for clients.

differences.title: 4. LATENCY FOR CLIENT WRITES
differences.leftDesc: Sending data to server requires new HTTP request, involving overhead.
differences.rightDesc: Messages sent over the open persistent connection have minimal overhead.

differences.title: 5. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Easier to implement for server-to-client updates, fewer edge cases to handle.
differences.rightDesc: Requires careful management of connection lifecycle, reconnections, and message handling.

differences.title: 6. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for broadcasting data from server. Think live scores or news updates.
differences.rightDesc: Perfect for applications needing rapid, bi-directional communication like multiplayer games or chats.

differences.title: 7. RESOURCE USAGE
differences.leftDesc: Can be more efficient if only server-to-client is needed. No constant open connections.
differences.rightDesc: Maintaining many open WebSocket connections can consume more server resources.
